> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **141** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6662e3f590e9790a28f598d3eb6f665e46f10703` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8327cddc2a0c0d2f34a0c30893524f889074cad2` — the merge of head `d09dffd8bfa4dd035daa612fbf5448bf9a8ea7b9` into base `6662e3f590e9790a28f598d3eb6f665e46f10703`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8327cddc2a0c0d2f34a0c30893524f889074cad2 && git checkout 8327cddc2a0c0d2f34a0c30893524f889074cad2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6662e3f590e9790a28f598d3eb6f665e46f10703 d09dffd8bfa4dd035daa612fbf5448bf9a8ea7b9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6662e3f590e9790a28f598d3eb6f665e46f10703 && git merge --no-ff d09dffd8bfa4dd035daa612fbf5448bf9a8ea7b9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6662e3f590e9790a28f598d3eb6f665e46f10703
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6662e3f590e9790a28f598d3eb6f665e46f10703` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bd8eff9eb6160fdbefcc1ff66b073eece047fa5d`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #23065 (body; triage 6128730227; claim 6129099833; os-dev-report 6131566986), PR #23092 (body, 13-file list, net diff `origin/main...bd8eff9eb6`, 568+/24-), and the 39 check-runs on the head. Read-only: `git` reads of the fetched PR ref and REST reads; no build, test, gate or ablation run here. The head is 7 commits behind `origin/main` (merge-base `275ad4229a`, main at `8c10776152`); the PR reads `mergeable: true`.

Check-runs on the head at 2026-10-12T20:07Z: 27 success (among them Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · CI release and engine gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Spec property liveness, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Build Core, Build Docs); 5 skipped by path filter (Console Pin Gate, the sharded Dogfood Regression Gate, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance); 7 STILL RUNNING: Test Core 1/6 through 6/6 and Type Check · workspace (the job that holds `check:api-surface`, `check:authorable-surface` and `check:docs`). The landing rule's all-green condition is checked at landing, not by this record; the dev reports the same gates green locally at this head.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Parse output — RIGHT. `ObjectSchema` and `ObjectExtensionSchema` run `materializeTreeSelfReferences` as an `.overwrite` after their refinements, writing the declaring object's name into `reference` on a `tree` field that names none. Against the triage ruling: the ruling's binding content is one reading, enforced, with no fallback in one reader; route (ii) satisfies it more strictly than editing the readers would — one helper, two object-aware doors, zero reader changes, and all 26 `referenceTargetOf` call sites plus the carrier-reading delete walk see an ordinary self-reference. The ruling's phrase "the engine's reference readers take the field's own object" is realised by handing the readers a field that names it; nothing in the ruling requires the readers themselves to change, and the ⛔ it does carry (no reader-side fallback) is honoured. Against `refuseForeignTreeReference`: its guidance "Drop `reference` (it is optional on a `tree`)" stays true at the input and now yields exactly the self-reference it promised; the refusal itself is untouched. Round trip: output is byte-identical to a field that wrote its own name (the key lands at `FieldSchema`'s shape position) and a re-parse is a no-op — both pinned in `tree-reference-self-only.test.ts`. A stored `sys_metadata` body keeps its bytes; the registry serves `getItem('object', name)` through `getObject` (the materialized merge), so a GET then PUT of `/meta/object` stores the own name, which the parse accepts. Diffs and `os validate`: a built artifact or `defineStack` output for such a field gains one key, the same class of change as the `deleteBehavior: set_null` materialization already on the field; `os validate` and `os lint` read that output, so the lint graph gains the edge. Authorable surface: unchanged — `reference` was already optional on `tree` and nothing new is accepted at the input; the input schema (`gen:schema`) does not move. Extension: `ObjectExtensionSchema` writes `extend`, which is right — the fields merge into that object (the #14892 refusal already judges a tree inside an extension against `extend`), and the engine registers an extension as `{ name: ext.extend, ... }` with ownership `extend` (`engine.ts` manifest loader), so the registry door stamps the same name.

2. The registry — RIGHT, one funnel. `registerObject` runs the same spec helper immediately after the field-type door and before `applySystemFields`, on a copy (`schema = { ...schema, fields }`; the helper copies the map and each stamped field), so the caller's definition is not mutated (pinned in `engine-cascade-delete-tree.test.ts`). It is a second SITE, not a second OPINION: same predicate, same output, no reader logic; the registry is the one choke point every door passes (declared stacks, manifests, the `saveMetaItem` write-through, the `sys_metadata` boot rehydration, raw `registerObject`), and the parse door is still needed for the authoring-time outputs (`defineStack`, `create()`, built artifacts, `os validate`). The one place that keeps the raw body — `applyObjectRegistryMutation` also calls `registerItem('object', item)` — is never read for objects, since `getItem` routes `object` to `getObject`. No ADR-0087 conversion entry is needed: no authorable key is added, aliased, renamed or retired; the stored shape stays legal and is materialized at every registration.

3. Door behaviour for a referenceless `tree`, each with its direction. The delete walk under the materialized default `set_null`: before, DELETE answered 200 and the child kept the deleted id; now 200 and the child's parent is null — the declared contract taking effect (pinned at the engine, the REST door and the metadata save door). `restrict`: before 200 and the delete went through; now 409 DELETE_RESTRICTED naming the tree's own object — a refusal at the delete door that did not exist, exactly the declared `deleteBehavior` (pinned, both doors). `cascade`: before children kept; now the subtree is deleted as one unit of work — a destructive widening at the delete door, exactly as declared (pinned). The write-time reference check: before, POST of a child naming a parent id that does not exist answered 201; now 400 `reference_not_found` — a NARROWING at the record write door, which is `assertReferencesResolve` doing for this field what it does for every reference field once `referenceTargetOf` answers (tabled in the PR, stated in the changeset, NOT pinned by a committed test). `expand=parent`: 404 to 200, and the nested relation filter: 400 to 200 — widenings at the read door (tabled, not pinned). The dangling audit and `os verify --delete-behaviors` now cover the field (the verify derivation is pinned). Clause-② line: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is RIGHT — the public surface grows by one export and the parse output gains a materialized key, while the published accept set (what the contract accepts or refuses) is unchanged. The write-door refusal does not call for the `(narrowing)` arm: by the repo's own rule the arm answers for the PUBLISHED contract surface and pulling the runtime back to the declared contract does not touch Clause-②, and the value a reference field may carry was always "an existing row of the target" — the field simply had no target before. Accordingly no ADR-0087 disposition is due (`check-adr-0087-registration` keys on `major`, a BREAKING banner, a `!` type or the narrowing arm; none applies, and the ledger governs authorable-shape migrations, of which there is none). The `Widens:` sentence is correct as scoped ("nothing that parsed before is refused"); it does not itself name the 201-to-400 change at the record door, which the body's table and the changeset's consumer-facing text do. Complete for the declaration's purpose; naming the record-door refusal in that sentence would have been tidier.

4. The new export `materializeTreeSelfReferences(ownName, fields)` — RIGHT. Reachable from `@objectstack/spec/data`: `src/data/index.ts` re-exports `object.zod`, `package.json` `exports['./data']` addresses it, and both `api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json` carry the symbol. Name states the act. Contract: generic over the field map, returns the same reference when nothing is written, otherwise a shallow copy with copied stamped fields; absence is `undefined`, `null` or empty string (the carrier reader's absence); a present value is untouched (a foreign one is the refusal's, a non-string one the carrier reader's); an array or a nameless call returns the input. A runtime helper in `packages/spec` sits inside the precedent of the exported `normalize*` parse helpers already there.

5. One judgment named WRONG, bounded: the two doors disagree on `reference: ''` on a `tree`. The parse door refuses it (`refuseForeignTreeReference` continues only on `undefined` or the own name, so an empty string is "a foreign target"), while the registry door — which never parses — rewrites it to the own name (the helper reads empty as absence, and the dev's test pins exactly that). So a raw registration or a metadata save carrying `reference: ''` is accepted and silently repaired where the contract refuses it. The effect is confined to a shape the contract already refuses at the authoring door, and before this PR the same shape read as "no target" at the registry, so no accepted input changes meaning; it is not a FAIL ground. See ③ item 10.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec`: `minor` — RIGHT. A new exported symbol on the published `./data` index is an additive widening of a public surface; under WHICH LEVEL in `pr-automation.yml` that is at least `minor`, and the `fix(` type cannot lower it. `@objectstack/objectql`: `patch` — RIGHT. `registry.ts` changes one import line and the body of `registerObject`; the exported signature `registerObject(schema, packageId?, namespace?, ownership, priority)` is unchanged, `index.ts` exports nothing new, and the registered definition now carrying a self-reference is a fix of what the registry hands its readers, not a new public symbol, key or value. The level axis (`check-changeset-no-major`) needs at least one moved package at `minor` on a `yes` declaration, and spec is it; Check Changeset and the Lint CI, release and engine gates run are green. `@objectstack/verify` publishes nothing here (one test file) and needs no changeset; `@objectstack/lint` is untouched; the docs are generated.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. Route (ii) completed at the registry instead of parse-only or reader-threading — ANSWERED, accepted. The measured necessity holds (the save door stores the body verbatim; a raw registration is never parsed), and the result is inside the triage's one-reading, no-fallback ruling. `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` is inside the claim's "engine's callers in `packages/objectql/src/` only as needed".
2. File surface: `registry.ts` not `engine.ts`; the door pin in `packages/verify/src` — ANSWERED, accepted: the card asked for the `bootStack` reading as the pin, and `bootStack` lives in verify.
3. The `user` sentence reworded rather than removed — ANSWERED, accepted: `DELETE_SEMANTICS_REFERENCE_TYPES` in `engine.ts` is exactly `master_detail`, `lookup`, `tree`, so `user` is outside the family and the substance was true.
4. Not merging `origin/main` before opening the PR — ESCALATED to the seat. AGENTS.md multi-agent discipline §10 says: before opening a PR, pull `main`, refresh build state and run the full suite once, and names the generated snapshots as the classic jointly-wrong artifact when `packages/spec` moved on either side. Measured here: 7 commits landed on `main` since the merge-base (three of them `feat(spec)`, one touching `registry.ts`); exactly two files are touched on both sides — `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` (main hunks at 2023 and 4594 to 4827; PR hunks at 1 and 2651: disjoint) and `content/docs/references/data/object.mdx` (main hunk at 456; PR hunks at 241 and 583: disjoint, and the file is generator-owned). A textual-disjointness reading is what §10 says is not a working-merge proof, and the incoming commits do touch the PR's packages, so the deviation is real. Compensations in place: the PR's check-runs ran on GitHub's merge ref against `main` at run time, and the queue rebuilds the PR as merged onto current `main` and re-runs the subscribing workflows, where `check:docs` reads the regenerated `object.mdx`. The seat decides: queue as is on the rebuilt-generation leg, or have the dev merge `origin/main`, rebuild spec and run `check:generated` and the suites, and push — which moves the head, and a merge commit is not a pure regeneration, so the record would be re-rendered.
5. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` where the dispatch spelled bare `yes` — ANSWERED, accepted: the arm is the closed-pair form `clause2-line.mjs` reads as the same widening, and the PR body and the changeset agree.
6. The 32-minute hold on the shared verify lock — noted for the lane; no action for this record.
7. objectui's use of `referenceTargetOf` and `referenceCarrierOf` NOT MEASURED (two 403s) — ANSWERED with a bound, residual named. Neither reader's signature or behaviour for a field that names a target changes, so a pinned checkout cannot break on a symbol. The shape a consumer now receives — a `tree` whose `reference` is its own object — is already in the shipped corpus (the showcase's `f_tree` writes it), so objectui has been receiving it; the residual is a reader that distinguishes a referenceless tree from a written one by key presence, which this review cannot rule out and the Console Pin Gate did not run on this PR. The seat can close the residual with one grep of `../objectui` at the pinned sha if it wants it closed.
8. The save-door lint judging the raw body — ANSWERED, accepted as a note. `assertRuntimeAuthoringRules` evaluates `AUTHORING_RULES` over the authored body before `registerObject`, and the object-graph rule reads `referenceTargetOf(def)`, so a referenceless `tree` inside the very object being saved contributes no edge in that one evaluation while `os validate` and `os lint` on `defineStack` output see it. The effect is a graph finding that cannot be raised at the save door, never a false refusal — the same class as every parse default the lint does not see. Not a contract violation under Prime Directive #10; the seat may file a lint-lane note if it wants the save door to lint the materialized body.
9. `ObjectSchema.create()` typed off the authored literal, and the verify dist race — ANSWERED, accepted as notes (the first is every parse default's property; the second is an environment property, observed once and green on re-run).
10. Found by this review, not raised by the dev: (a) the `reference: ''` door disagreement in ① item 5 — carrier: none; a one-line tightening (stamp only `undefined` and `null`, leave the empty string to the carrier reader as before) would make the registry door refuse-or-ignore exactly what the parse refuses; dedupe words: tree reference empty string registry parse disagree. (b) Three door readings the PR tables — write check 201 to 400, expand 404 to 200, nested relation filter 400 to 200 — are measured but not pinned by a committed test; the card's acceptance asked for the `bootStack` delete pins only, so this is not a gap in the card, and the seat may ask for the write-check pin since that reading is the one refusal added at a data door. (c) Seven check-runs are still in progress at the stamp (Test Core 1 to 6, Type Check · workspace); this record does not wait on them, and the landing step reads them.

Adopted by `domain:engine` seat 2 at 2026-10-12T20:10Z, after a tool-use audit of the isolated reviewer's transcript: reads, `git fetch` into a review ref, scratch files inside this PR's scratch directory, and one record write. It made no GitHub write and ran no build, test or gate.
